title: Station to station
why: Two phones on one cluster. CUCM does the signaling. RTP goes phone to phone unless a media resource is inserted.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Phone A sends the INVITE to the subscriber that holds its registration.

steps.label: 100 Trying
steps.note: CUCM has the INVITE and is doing digit analysis.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The called CSS and partition resolved to Phone B.

steps.label: 180 Ringing
steps.note: Phone B is alerting. This is still signaling, not audio.

steps.label: 180 Ringing
steps.note: CUCM relays alerting to the caller.

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.note: Phone B answered. SDP names the phone's own media address.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio goes phone to phone. It does not hairpin through CUCM.

title: PSTN through CUBE
why: CUBE is a B2BUA. The Call-ID changes there. A 200 OK on the trunk does not prove the phone has audio.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The line CSS must contain the partition of the route pattern, or this number does not exist.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The pattern points at a route list, then a route group, then the SIP trunk. This Call-ID is the CUCM leg.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: A dial-peer matches. CUBE starts a new Call-ID toward the carrier.
Ringing on the carrier leg. Relay it back only after you know which leg you are looking at.
CUBE notifies CUCM. Still no audio.

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.note: The carrier answered. SDP is the carrier media address.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Phone media goes to CUBE, not through CUCM, unless an MTP or transcoder is actually invoked.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: CUBE anchors or relays media toward the carrier. Prove both RTP legs.

title: Webex Calling local gateway
why: Webex Calling still needs a premises border for your own PSTN. Calling Plan has no local gateway. This path does.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The client signals Webex Calling, not your old subscriber.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Outbound PSTN uses the local gateway trunk or registration, on the ports that design chose.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Dial-peers on the gateway decide the carrier leg.

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.note: Answer is on the carrier leg. Check that SDP before you blame the app.

steps.label: 200 OK
steps.note: The gateway completes the Webex leg.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media for this PSTN call anchors at the local gateway. The cloud signaling path is not the audio path.

title: UCCE comprehensive
why: Ingress, prompt, script, queue, and agent are the contact. CUIC is the report beside that path, not the audio.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The carrier hits the border. This leg has its own Call-ID.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: CVP takes the call for treatment.

steps.label: New call
steps.note: ICM runs the script. The route request is not RTP.

steps.label: Prompt
steps.note: VVB plays the menu. A prompt is not a queue.

steps.label: Label
steps.note: The script returns a label for an agent or a queue.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The agent phone is a CUCM destination.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: If the phone rings and Finesse does not, look at PG, CTI, and Finesse.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio is between the caller path and the agent phone. CUIC never carries it.

steps.label: Interval
steps.note: Join the report with RouterCallKey and matching time. A skill rename can break history while calls still connect.
